A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same research work despite the changed title. All supplied pages are readable, but v1 ends after its references without the appendices cited in Sections 4–5, limiting verification of those supplementary analyses. V2 includes Appendices A–E.

before.justification: V1 reports original training-regime experiments, accuracy–computation curves, representation analyses, and classifier-size and placement studies in Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 reports original vision and NLP experiments, diagnostic analyses, ablations, and convergence measurements, with additional results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The original two-phase mixed procedure remains, but Appendix A introduces mixed-gradual training. It progressively optimizes the last i classifiers across multiple phases, keeps weights unfrozen, and uses early stopping to advance. This adds a substantive training procedure beyond the original joint, disjoint, and mixed regimes.

E1.justification: V2 expands beyond vision classification to 20-Newsgroups text classification and STS-B regression, and adds TinyImageNet evaluation. It also reports direct ImageNet-1k classification experiments. Imagenette remains in Table 20, while CIFAR-10 remains in the mode-connectivity and loss-landscape analyses; neither should be treated as removed.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds evaluated branch-wise, separate, and alternating training comparators. V2 also evaluates PBEE and entropy-based exiting, and adds SDN and increasing/decreasing loss-weighting comparisons alongside gradient equilibrium. The retained Imagenette head-size experiment gains disjoint-regime rows in Table 20, absent from v1 Table 2.

E3.justification: V2 adds MSDNet, ResNet-50, BERT, and ViT-S configurations and no longer reports the EfficientNetV2-s experiment. Placement controls change from ViT every-1/2/3 and first/last-four arrangements to ResNet-50 every-1 through every-5 and asymmetric arrangements. Regression introduces MSE evaluation. One setting remains ambiguous: identical ResNet-50 results are labeled 25% budget in Table 1 but 35% in Table 11.

E4.justification: V2 adds gradient-dominance and mode-connectivity analyses, convergence-time comparisons, and expanded loss-weighting and classifier-size/placement studies. V1's learning-rate and undertrained-backbone analysis in Section 5.3 and Figure 11 is not retained. The loss-landscape analysis survives in Appendix B, so its relocation is not a removal.

E5.justification: The reported replication changes from four different seeds in v1 to three runs in v2 Section 4.1. Mean and standard-deviation reporting continues in Appendix C, although the new TinyImageNet ablations in Tables 6–7 lack corresponding uncertainty tables. V2 also discloses Monte Carlo estimation of mutual information. These statements do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E6.justification: V2 supplies extensive new benchmark, comparator, and diagnostic results. For example, Table 1 reports ImageNet-1k ViT-T accuracy at 100% budget of 71.20% mixed, 68.39% joint, and 71.61% disjoint. Conversely, all 30 mean/standard-deviation pairs from v1 Table 2 remain unchanged in v2 Table 20. EfficientNet and undertrained-backbone results disappear; results under new configurations are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 add a formal gradient-dominance definition and a permutation-alignment optimization with an interpolated parameter path for mode connectivity. These materially expand the mathematical analysis beyond v1. The loss-landscape equation is retained in Appendix B, while v1's explicit gradient-rescaling equation is omitted. No formal theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 elevates the diagnostic framework to a central contribution and explicitly claims generalization across modalities, classification, regression, and exit criteria. Its conclusion strengthens the gradient-scaling finding into a claim that scaling is unnecessary with mixed training. It also recommends mixed training particularly for medium/high budgets, replacing v1's contradictory concluding recommendation for easy inputs and early exits.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking deeper-classifier gradient dominance and mode connectivity to mixed training's behavior, and interprets classifier capacity as dependent on the training regime. It reconciles the concluding budget recommendations with the earlier mutual-information discussion and identifies shared-backbone circumstances favoring disjoint training. However, the explicit warning about mixed training failing with an undertrained backbone is removed.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix E newly document optimizer, scheduler, batch sizes, learning rates, weight decay, patience, augmentations, model dimensions, exit positions, sequence lengths, and ImageNet hardware. These substantially improve reproducibility without establishing changes to previously undocumented settings. The code repository remains the same; v1's explicit 100-threshold sweep and best-checkpoint restoration description are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around conditional computation, classifier cascades, distillation, ensembling, and training–inference mismatch. Section 5 acknowledges SDN's consideration of both joint and disjoint training and a concurrent comparison by Bae et al., qualifying the novelty as broad systematic analysis. Appendix A additionally relates alternative regimes to BERxiT and LayerSkip.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, updates the author block, and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Related work moves after the experiments, the analytical framework is separated from its empirical evaluation, and supporting material is organized into Appendices A–E. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Budget tables become the principal performance presentation, with additional curves grouped in Appendix D. New gradient-dominance and mode-connectivity figures are added, the loss landscapes are redrawn and relocated, and v1's two-panel numerical-rank figure is reduced to the retained backbone-versus-mixed panel.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens generalizability and reproducibility through NLP/regression tests, broader regime comparisons, diagnostic analyses, and concrete training specifications in Appendix E. It also fixes v1's conflicting concluding guidance. These gains outweigh losing the undertraining study and reducing the stated run count. Qualifications remain necessary: Appendix A's blanket mixed-gradual advantage is contradicted by its worse 20-Newsgroups results in Table 13.
